## Reading

Loukissas, Chapter 1, _Local Origins_, pp. 13–26. [Session 4](04-what-does-local-mean.qmd) reads the same chapter from a different angle.

## Reading summary

The chapter challenges common ideas about data. Data are plural and heterogeneous, not universal or context-free. Things become data through acts of interpretation, recording, and use. Data are also material: databases, categories, formats, and instruments shape what can be recorded and what can be done with it. Turning something into data always changes it and can remove parts of the original context.

## In class

Students identify the decisions that sit behind a simple table.
